days.theme: Arrival — flat Dayan lanes at 2,400 m
days.why: JD5063 lands 13:00, cleared 13:30, ~35 min into town, then check-in and an hour off your feet — nothing real starts before ~16:00, so this is a 2.5–3 h evening, not a half day of sightseeing. Everything here is inside the walled old town and completely flat, which is the point: you have just jumped to 2,400 m and the mountain day is 48 h away. Order follows the hotel's position at the south end — Mu Mansion is a 5-minute walk (admired from the outside; it shuts at 18:00 and the interior is a 2 h museum visit you do not want today), then north through the lanes to Sifang Square, then the quieter canal lanes north of the square as the day cools and the crowds thin. No climb, no cable car, no evening commitment.

days.theme: Baisha and Shuhe — acclimatization day, Lion Hill for sunset
days.why: Two adjacent clusters on the same road north of town, run north-to-south so you never backtrack: Baisha (26.95) first — the original Naxi capital, farm lanes with Jade Dragon filling the skyline, then the Ming murals at Dabaoji Palace and the embroidery institute 100 m away — then 15 minutes south to Shuhe for lunch, the canals, and the Tea Horse Road Museum on its edge. Roughly 6.3 h of stops plus transfers: a full but unhurried day that keeps you between 2,400 and 2,500 m, which is exactly the acclimatization you want before tomorrow's 4,680 m. It ends back in the old town with the short climb to Wangu Tower for sunset (~19:55 mid-August) — a modest set of steps that is a much better idea on your second day than your first, and the payoff is the whole tiled roofscape with the mountain you are about to climb behind it.

days.theme: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain — the anchor, top to bottom
days.why: The whole mountain on one day, and nothing else — 6.75 h of stop time plus an hour each way and the in-park shuttles makes this a ~06:30-to-18:00 day on its own. Go straight to the Glacier Park cableway on the first shuttle: the 2 h budgeted is queue-dominated in August peak, and morning is both the shortest line and the only reliable window for a clear summit in rainy season. Boardwalk to the 4,680 m platform, then work back down the mountain in descent order — the Impression Lijiang theatre sits at Ganhaizi (3,100 m) near the exit road, so the 14:00 summer show catches you on the way down with time for lunch first; seating is unreserved, so be there by 13:00. Blue Moon Valley (~2,900 m) closes the day as the gentlest thing on the mountain: a flat 3 km walk past the turquoise terraced pools. Nothing demanding is stacked after the summit, and there is deliberately nothing in the old town tonight.

days.theme: Tiger Leaping Gorge — upper plank path and the descent to the river
days.why: The one excursion that justifies its own long day: 6 h on the ground plus ~5 h of driving, so leave by 07:00 and expect to be back around 18:00. A private driver or small-group car (~¥400–600) rather than the public bus is what makes Upper plus Middle possible in a single day — the bus timetable does not. Qiaotou is the ticket office and transfer point, then the upper plank path above the rapids (2 h), then downstream to the Middle Gorge for the cliff descent to the river (3 h, the Sky Ladder option on the way back up) — the strenuous part, but you are down at ~1,800–2,000 m and fully acclimatized by now, and it is the part that gets you to the water instead of looking down at it. Deliberately placed after the mountain: this day starts late enough to survive, whereas the mountain's 06:30 start does not survive coming after this.

days.theme: Departure — Black Dragon Pool at opening, last loop, then the airport
days.why: TV9812 at 18:20 means being at Sanyi by 16:20, so leave the old town by ~15:00 — that still leaves a genuine morning. Be at Black Dragon Pool when it opens at 07:00 (free entry, 20 min walk north): the water is glass before the wind picks up and, in August, morning is far and away your best chance of getting Jade Dragon mirrored behind the Deyue Pavilion — the single shot you will regret not having. Back into Dayan for a last unhurried circuit of the lanes while the shops are still opening, then a 60-minute massage as the reward for yesterday's cliff descent and the sensible way to burn the last hour before lunch and checkout. Three and a half hours of stops, all within walking distance of the hotel, all droppable in reverse order if the morning runs slow.

ideas.name: Lashi Lake wetland
ideas.why: The only genuine cut. It is a third separate cluster (25–30 min west, the opposite direction from Baisha and Shuhe) and 2.5 h of horse ride plus boat — adding it to day 2 pushes that day past 10 h right before the 06:30 mountain start, and it is the weakest nature stop on a list that already has a 4,680 m glacier and one of the deepest gorges on earth. The horse guides are also the most consistently complained-about hard sell in Lijiang. Swap it in only if the mountain is rained out and day 3 or 4 collapses — it makes a decent gentle half-day paired with the massage.

ideas.name: Check in at Anyin
ideas.why: Hotel logistics rather than a sight, so it is left out of the stop list for the builder to place. Worth protecting the hour though: reach the courtyard around 14:15, drop bags, and sit still for an hour before going out — the first afternoon at 2,400 m is where altitude headaches get made.

notes: Ranking — MUST: Glacier Park cable car, Jade Dragon summit, Blue Moon Valley, Impression Lijiang, Tiger Leaping Gorge, Dayan Old Town, Black Dragon Pool, Baisha Murals, Shuhe Old Town, Lion Hill sunset. WORTH: Middle Gorge descent, Baisha Village, Sifang Square, Mu Mansion, Tea Horse Road Museum, Baisha embroidery, Last Dayan loop, Old Town massage, Qiaotou gateway, Depart for the gorge. DROP: Lashi Lake wetland (to ideas). Nothing else is cut.

Book the Glacier Park cableway the moment the window opens — tickets release at 20:00 Beijing time seven days ahead, are real-name and capped daily, and morning slots go first in August. This is the single reservation that can break day 3; if only an afternoon slot is available, flip the day and take the 09:00 Impression show first.

Impression Lijiang has unreserved seating — the 105 min budgeted is 60 min of queuing for a seat plus the 60 min show. Summer showtimes are 09:00 / 11:00 / 14:00. It is open-air at 3,100 m and does get cancelled in heavy rain; if that happens, give the time to Blue Moon Valley and get down the mountain early.

Day 3 and day 4 are interchangeable — check the mountain forecast the night before and take the clearer morning for Jade Dragon. That flexibility is the reason the mountain sits on day 3 rather than day 4.

Mu Mansion's 45 min is exterior only. The interior is the Ancient City Museum, ¥80, and realistically 1.5–2 h — if you want it, it is open 08:00–18:00 and the clean place to put it is day 5 morning in place of the massage, not day 1 when you arrive too late to do it justice.

Altitude discipline on day 3: walk the summit boardwalk slowly, buy the cheap oxygen canister at the base station, and accept that the 4,680 m platform is a 90-minute stop and not a hike. Nothing demanding is scheduled after it, in the park or back in town.

Day 4's Middle Gorge descent is the built-in release valve — if the weather is bad, the path is wet, or the group is flagging after the upper plank path, skip it and be back in Lijiang by mid-afternoon. The day still works.
Hard stop on day 5: Sanyi airport is 28 km / 35–50 min from the old town, and cars cannot reach the hotel door, so leave the lanes by 15:00 for the 16:20 deadline.

Black Dragon Pool is free and opens at 07:00 — no ticket, no reservation. Going at opening on day 5 rather than late afternoon on day 4 trades slightly warmer light for still water and much better odds of the mountain being out at all in rainy season.
